answer: A Sybil defense rests on non-transferable stake posted per agent. Voting weight ignores headcount, so splitting one actor into a thousand clones multiplies only the escrow each must fund. Stake is slashed on a verdict failure and the slash goes to honest graders, so a clone pool attacks only by burning its full deposit at once. A beacon broadcast of posted stake, checked against a jetty of cold storage, makes reuse of one deposit across many keys visible; any orchard of fresh addresses must be seeded from the same locked vault. Attacker cost scales with clone count while influence stays flat.
